notes: PHASE 9 (OBLIVION-PLAN section 8.3): the things a docker FIGHTS in. Read after items_consumables.json and appended to the registry, because items.json is the owner's and is never edited; every row here comes after every row there, so no saved or hashed index of an earlier row moves.
Same columns as items.json, plus grip and model. slot adds offhand (a shield, and nothing else in this build) and hands (gloves).

grip is how a hand row is held: one or two. A two-handed row bares the other hand when it goes on, and a shield put on bares a two-handed row out of the hand (Kit::wear). An offhand row is always a shield. No other row names a grip.
Reach and speed are the GRIP's, never the row's (items.hpp gripTiming): one-handed is the shipped swing to the step, two-handed reaches a tile and five eighths and recovers a third slower.
damage on a hand row here is the row's OWN span, the one the player's blow rolls: at least one, low before high, no wider than eight. items.json's rows keep their class's span; these need not.
dr is flat damage reduction while worn, summed over every slot but the hand: a shield and a pair of gloves count like a coat. The floor of one point through any kit holds.

model is the render key: which prop the world, the viewmodel and the figure draw. Never hashed, never read by a rule. The cutlass and the mace are items.json's own rows (their ids are taken there), so they carry no model; their stands are here.

stands: a sea-chest's worth set out on the quay's north-east corner, where the boats put in, beside the boots items.json already stands at (158,61). Nobody's. Kept clear of the Tarwalk tiles the phase 8 crosshair cases stand on (152-156, 62-64).

Weights are in items.json's scale and each named loadout fits the base sheet's 240: a cap, a gambeson and a cutlass (83); the iron pot, the brigandine, the gauntlets, the round shield, the mace and the boots (212); the pot, the brigandine, the gauntlets and the maul (182).
Provenance: no canon row names these. A slop chest's run of quayside arms and harness, nothing a docker could not have seen come off a boat.
